channel.title: BudgetGo Blog
channel.description: Practical guides on budgeting, tracking spending, and getting the most out of BudgetGo.

item.title: How to Track Apple Pay Spending Automatically (Step by Step)
item.description: How to track Apple Pay spending automatically with an Apple Shortcuts automation: set it up in about two minutes, see what gets captured, and fix it when a payment doesn't show up.

item.title: How Much Does Thanksgiving Dinner Cost? (Budget Per Person, With the Math)
item.description: How much Thanksgiving dinner costs in 2026, and how to set your own budget per person: a worked example for 10 guests, ways to trim the bill, and how to track it before Thursday, November 26.

item.title: How BudgetGo Finds Your Subscriptions and Bills Before They Hit
item.description: How to track subscriptions and recurring bills automatically: how BudgetGo spots repeating charges, lines up what's due this week, and helps you plan before the money leaves.

item.title: How Much Should You Spend on Black Friday? (With a Budget Example)
item.description: How much to spend on Black Friday, worked out from your own numbers: set a ceiling, build a ranked list, cap impulse buys, and track every deal so the sales don't wreck your December.

item.title: How Much Should You Spend on Christmas Gifts? (With the Math)
item.description: How much to spend on Christmas gifts, worked out from your own numbers: set a total you can afford, split it per person and per child, and track it so December doesn't spill into January.

item.title: How to Track Your Spending Without a Spreadsheet
item.description: A simple 4-step system to track your spending automatically, sort it into categories, and spot where your money goes, no spreadsheet needed.

item.title: How to Find and Cancel Subscriptions You Forgot About
item.description: A quick subscription audit: how to find every recurring charge, check App Store subscriptions, decide what to cancel, and stop surprise renewals.

item.title: The 50/30/20 Budget Rule, Explained With a Real Example
item.description: What the 50/30/20 budget rule is, how to split your take-home pay into needs, wants, and savings, and how to adjust it when rent is high.
